title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 380 (Documents, etc., to be delivered to Registrar by foreign companies)

content.overview: Every foreign company shall, within thirty days of the establishment of its place of business in India, deliver to the Registrar for registration: (a) a certified copy of the charter, statutes or memorandum and articles, or other instrument constituting or defining the constitution of the company (with a certified English translation if not in English); (b) the full address of the registered or principal office; (c) a list of the directors and secretary with prescribed particulars; (d) the name and address of one or more persons resident in India authorised to accept service of process and notices; (e) the full address of the office in India deemed to be its principal place of business in India; (f) particulars of opening and closing of a place of business in India on earlier occasions; (g) a declaration that none of the directors or the authorised representative has been convicted or debarred from formation of companies and management in India or abroad; and (h) any other prescribed information. Existing foreign companies that had not delivered the corresponding documents under the 1956 Act remain under that obligation.
content.glance: Within 30 days of establishing a place of business in India, a foreign company must file constitution documents, addresses, director/secretary list, authorised local agent, prior place-of-business particulars, and the prescribed declaration.
content.study: Section 380 is the initial registration duty for foreign companies that establish a place of business in India. The filing window is thirty days. The section lists the constitutional, address, personnel, service-agent, and declaration particulars that must be delivered. Alterations and continuing obligations are addressed in related provisions; failure is treated as a continuing default under the Chapter’s penalty scheme.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Within 30 days of establishing a place of business in India, a foreign company must deliver to the Registrar the constitution documents, addresses, director/secretary list, authorised Indian agent, prior place-of-business particulars, and the prescribed declaration.

provisions.title: Documents, etc., to be delivered to Registrar by foreign companies

examples.title: Illustration — s. 380
examples.body: A UK company opens a branch office in Mumbai and, within thirty days, files its memorandum, registered-office address, director list, and the name of an authorised person resident in India under s. 380.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 380?
hypotheticals.analysis: It requires foreign companies establishing a place of business in India to deliver specified documents to the Registrar within thirty days.

rows.left: Documents to be delivered on establishment

misconceptions.trap: Treating a foreign company as a company under s. 2(20) merely because it files under s. 380.
misconceptions.correction: Filing under s. 380 does not incorporate the foreign company in India; it remains a foreign company.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 380 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm establishment of a place of business in India. II. Check the 30-day filing window and listed documents. III. Conclude on compliance.
